Tokyo
October 29, 195k
Dear Girls, Family and Friends,
I think my last letter covered our
arrival Tokyo on October 21st.
Since
then in a business way we
have been more or less stymied by politics all same like home.
The Premier Yoshida was re-elected but his margin in the Diet was
smell and opposition in his own and other parties large.
I do not
even pretend to understand Japanese polities but it seems
the op-
position is clamoring for the scalps of
some of our most influential
friends in high places. Until the new Cebinet is selected and
approved by the Diet no one will do anything. In fact,
they con't
and won't even
mernibile, our hotel del hrs descended to
en area of petty bickering and we
are occupied mostly with smell
affairs dealt in by small people.
We hope within a week or ten days
to move it up on the plateau of high endeavor.
Japen is booming.
Everyone is working
Building end rebuilding are everywhere in evidence.
businesses are
being re-established.
New ones are being formed.
There is feverish activity in shipbuilding, textiles, cement pro-
duction, steel mills, menufacturing of all kinds.
No doubt there
are those - and I don't blame them a bit - who will never forgive
Japen or the Japanese for the way in which the war was conducted.
However, I think we must look to U.S. interests down through the
first and foremost. Not a single Japinese Conmunist won
a seat in the recent elections.
If we have to fight Russia and/or
Chins at some time in the future - God forbid - one of our strongest
and most loyal allies will be Japen. I do not meen to be an
apologist for Japan, but it is true that the militarists here were
the ones to blame for most of the atrocities.
They, as their counter-
parts in Germany, do not represent e true cross-section of the people.
In thet connection,
the firing of MacArthur had what I am sure was
a wholly unanticipated effect upon the Japanese.
We had been
talking against militerism beforeand after V-J Day but our prope-
genda was not going over very well. While we condemned the military
we ourselves had instelled the grentest American military leader -
General MacArthur - as Supreme Commander over all the Japanese.
Then when he - the Grent Emperor who out-Emperored 'em all and out-
Caesered Caeser - was fired by a second grade unsuccessful civilian
haberdasher who happened to hold the political U.S. helm at the
moment, the Jops were suddenly made aware that we really practiced

what we nreached - that in the U.S. the pen was indeed nightier
It had a good effect here in Japan and
Hirohito n chance to resume his post as Emperor which he would
never have had with MacArthur on hand.
Last weekend ve motored up to
Karuizawa with the Shermans who have a cottage there.
It is a
mountain resort ebout 100 miles northwest of Tokyo where the foreign
residents go in summer to escape the heat and din of Tokyo.
the very great inventions here would be a hornless automobile.
would help solve their over-population problem and give the poor
city dweller some respite from
the incessant clamor.
was lovely.
The Fall colors not as varigated as lake George but
the reds of the Japanese maples more brilliant then at home.
was interesting, too, going along the road through smell towns and
open country.
On the 28th we celebrated the Twenty-
Fifth Anniversery of the founding of PAA with the showing of e Pan
Americen historical film.
Japanese staff with their wives and
children were on hand and the party ended up with ice cream and
coke and also a "presento" for each of the kids. You never saw as
cute kids in all your life or as well behaved.
This weekend we're going to motor down
to Hakone where there is a good hotel on
the edge of the lake with
a fine close-up view of Fuji. Debby has been in Jopen several tines
the sacred mountain.
The jinx may continue through
the weekend but we're hoping for one or two clear days. It should be
beautiful this time of the year with weather much like our seme
months at home.
Tonight we are to be the guests of
honor at a dinner party which the Dellas Shermons are giving in
our honor.
They built a house of their own when they could not
find one to rent.
He is s former Colonel in the Army Air Force
and
now ects as Far Estern #1 for PAA.
Will write agoin soon end hope then
to give you some idea es to our plans and schedule. Meanwhile, our
very best.
H. M. B.
